title: DELTA4: Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication for Low Sparsity
claim: Our method beats the dense baseline at far lower sparsity than existing approaches, and is fastest across the whole range.
layout: 1 line plot, runtime vs sparsity, hatched highlight region, arrow annotations
description: A single line chart of runtime in microseconds (y-axis, 0–1400) against sparsity percent (x-axis, 0–95). A flat blue cuBLAS line sits near 950 µs and represents the dense baseline. Four colored lines show the sparse methods. The green MACKO line descends steadily from about 1230 µs and crosses the dense line at about 25% sparsity. The purple Sputnik, red DASP and orange cuSPARSE lines fall steeply and only cross the dense line at 65%, about 70% and 71%. A yellow-green diagonally hatched region fills the gap between MACKO and the other curves. Black arrows with labels (25%, 65%, 71%) mark the crossover points. A legend sits at lower left. The eye goes first to the hatched wedge and the green line.
caption: Sparse matrix–vector multiplication runtime. Matrix size 36864, 12288 in fp16 on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU. Using MACKO, sparse computation exceeds the performance of dense at sparsity as low as 25%. Existing libraries require 2.6× fewer non-zeros to achieve the same performance. The improvement of this work is displayed as highlighted region.
abstract: Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) is a fundamental operation in the inference of sparse Large Language Models (LLMs). Because existing SpMV methods perform poorly under the low and unstructured sparsity (30-90%) commonly observed in pruned LLMs, unstructured pruning provided only limited memory reduction and speedup. We propose MACKO-SpMV, a GPU-optimized format and kernel co-designed to reduce storage overhead while preserving compatibility with the GPU's execution model. This enables efficient SpMV for unstructured sparsity without specialized hardware units (e.g., tensor cores) or format-specific precomputation. Empirical results show that at sparsity 50%, MACKO is the first approach with significant 1.5x memory reduction and 1.2-1.5x speedup over dense representation. Speedups over other SpMV baselines: 2.8-13.0x over cuSPARSE, 1.9-2.6x over Sputnik, and 2.2-2.5x over DASP. Applied to Llama2-7B pruned with Wanda to sparsity 50%, it delivers 1.5x memory reduction and 1.5x faster inference at fp16 precision. Thanks to MACKO, unstructured pruning at 50% sparsity is now justified in real-world LLM workloads.
